verdict.rationale: Airbyte documents official MCP servers connecting agents like Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, and Codex to its data pipelines, with a dedicated 'connect-ask-act' concept page describing natural-language querying/acting on data via agents, and an AI Assistant that auto-configures connector builder fields. This supports natural-language operation of data connections/agents, but it's scoped mainly to data querying/connector setup rather than full conversational control of platform administration (syncs, scheduling, workspace management), and there's no independent/hands-on corroboration of the MCP or AI Assistant experience. Missing for 10: independent user validation of MCP/agent natural-language control, evidence that broader platform operations (not just data queries/connector building) can be driven by natural language.
